Checklists

Bringing Home Your First Kitten

Before the kitten arrives

    Home safety

    • Install "anti-cat" safety nets on windows.
    • Secure windows set to tilt-open ventilation mode.
    • Move electrical cords out of reach.
    • Store household chemicals and medications out of reach.
    • Remove toxic houseplants.
    • Check for narrow gaps behind furniture and appliances.
    • Secure tall furniture and shelves.
    • Remove small objects, threads, rubber bands, and bags.
    • Make high places safe to prevent falls.

    Essential supplies

      Litter box

      • Litter box.
      • Litter.
      • Scoop.
      • Litter mat.

      Food and water (1 or more of each)

      • Food bowl.
      • Water bowl or fountain.
      • Food the kitten was already eating.
      • Treats.

      Sleep and rest

      • Bed.
      • Blanket.
      • Hideout or house.

      Play

      • Scratching post.
      • Wand toy.
      • Balls.
      • Interactive toys.

      For transport

      • Carrier.
      • Absorbent pad.
      • ID tag (if needed).

      First day at home

      • Open the carrier and let the kitten come out on its own.
      • Show it where the litter box is.
      • Show it the food and water bowls.
      • Don't introduce the whole apartment at once — start with one room and open up more space as the kitten shows interest.
      • Avoid picking it up unless necessary.
      • Let it explore the space calmly.
      • Don't invite guests on the first day.

      First 7 days

      • Feed the food it's used to.
      • Don't switch litter.
      • Stick to a feeding schedule.
      • Play daily, 10–20 minutes per session.
      • Monitor its appetite.
      • Monitor its water intake.
      • Monitor its bowel movements and urination.
      • Gradually introduce the rest of the rooms.

      Veterinary care

      • Schedule an initial checkup.
      • Check for a microchip.
      • Check the vaccination schedule.
      • Discuss parasite prevention.
      • Ask about a recommended diet.

      If you have other pets at home

      • Prepare a separate room.
      • Separate bowls.
      • Separate litter box.
      • Don't introduce the animals right away.
      • Do regular scent swapping between the animals using scented items.
      • Gradually arrange their first meetings.

      After the adjustment period

      • Choose a suitable food.
      • Set up a feeding routine.
      • Set up vertical space.
      • Get additional scratching posts.
      • Schedule spaying or neutering (based on age and your vet's recommendations).
      • Create a digital pet passport.

      Not a substitute for a vet

      The information in this app comes from open sources and the experience of cat owners. It does not replace a consultation or an examination by a vet. Decisions about your pet's health and care are the owner's to make — if in any doubt, contact a vet.
